If he likes cold drinks (closer to ice cube temp) get him steel, if he like just a chill put on the drink get stone ones. If buying steel ones make sure they guarantee no metallic taste.

The steel is over twice as dense as the granite, so I'd go with that. More density equals more capacity to chill the drink. Steel also has better heat transfer than granite, so they'll chill it faster.

https://www.yourbestdigs.com/reviews/best-whiskey-stones/

https://coolmaterial.com/feature/we-tested-a-bunch-of-whiskey-stones-to-see-which-were-the-best/

Don't confuse heat transfer with heat capacity.

Steel will transfer heat faster, but metals often have very little heat capacity - that's why they're such good heat conductors.

According to https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/specific-heat-capacity-d_391.html

Steel has a specific heat of 490 J/kg°C while granite has 790. That means that the stones take up more heat per kilogram, and granite stones will eventually end up in cooler whiskey. Eventually. Because steel conducts heat faster, it only matters if you're letting your whiskey sit for a minute or two.

Ultimately I think it's just a matter of preference. I like the texture of granite more than steel, and I doubt the other numbers can actually be detected unless you're directly comparing them.
